what: The Credit Card Payoff Calculator shows how long it will take to clear a card balance with a fixed monthly payment, and how much interest you will pay on the way. It also works backwards: give it a number of months and it tells you the monthly payment needed to be debt free by then.

It is for anyone carrying a balance on a credit card or store card who wants a clear plan. You can see how much faster you pay off the card, and how much interest you save, by paying a little more each month.
The calculation runs in your browser. Results are estimates and not financial advice.
uses: See the exact number of months your current payment needs.
See the cost of minimum payments
Enter a small payment to see how much interest it costs over time.
Use "Months to be debt free" to find the payment needed for your goal.
Try 150 and 250 to see how much time and interest you save.
Enter the new, lower APR to compare it with your current card.
tutorial: Type what you owe in "Card balance". The default is 5000.
Type the yearly rate in "Interest rate (APR %)", for example 22. You can find it on your statement.
Type the fixed amount you plan to pay each month in "Monthly payment". It must be more than one month of interest, or the balance will never go down.
"Time to pay off" shows years and months, such as "2 yrs 1 mo". "Total interest" is all interest paid, and "Total paid" is the balance plus interest.
Under "Pay it off by a target date", type a number of months (1 to 600) in "Months to be debt free". The box below shows "Pay X a month", the fixed payment that clears the balance in that time.
Change the payment or the target months and the results update at once.
features: Each month the tool adds interest of balance × APR ÷ 12 ÷ 100, then takes off your payment. The last month only pays what is left, so the totals are exact.
If your payment is not more than the first month’s interest, a message shows that interest amount and asks you to pay more.
The payment for a target is balance × r ÷ (1 − (1 + r) to the power −months), with r = APR ÷ 12 ÷ 100, the same formula used for loans.
Payoff time is shown in an easy format like "1 yr 2 mo".
See the real cost of carrying the balance.
All numbers update as you type.

example.title: Worked example: a 3,000 balance at 20% APR
example.text: You owe 3000 at 20% APR. The first month’s interest is 3000 × 20 ÷ 12 ÷ 100 = 50.00, so you must pay more than 50. Paying 150 a month, the "Time to pay off" is "2 yrs 1 mo" (25 months), "Total interest" is 679.82 and "Total paid" is 3,679.82. Raise the payment to 250 and it takes "1 yr 2 mo" with only 375.49 in interest. To be debt free in 12 months, type 12 in "Months to be debt free" and the tool says "Pay 277.90 a month".

tips: Stop using the card while you pay it off; new purchases are not included in this plan.
Even a small extra payment each month can save a lot of interest.
Paying a high-APR card first saves the most money if you have several cards.
Your card may charge interest daily, so real totals can differ a little.
Re-check the plan if your APR changes or a promotional rate ends.
problems: It says the payment does not cover the monthly interest
Your payment is equal to or less than balance × APR ÷ 12. Pay more than the amount shown in the message.
Balance and monthly payment must be above 0 and the APR must be 0 or more.
The target box shows a dash
Type a whole number of months from 1 to 600, and make sure the balance is filled in.
My card statement shows a different payoff time
Card issuers may use daily interest, fees or minimum payments that change with the balance. This tool uses a fixed monthly payment.
